newsitem.title: USA: AOL charging firms in Company Connection.
newsitem.headline: AOL charging firms in Company Connection.

text.p: America Online Inc said it will begin charging firms in a forum on AOL called Company Connection, an information area made up of over 200 technology firms, as it moves to a more profitable business model.

Previously, this area had been free to all of the firms with a presence in the Company Connection, ranging from tiny, unknown start-ups, to giants like International Business Machines Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co.
"It's really a question of creating a business model that is right and right for the future," said Myer Berlow, senior vice president of advertising at America Online.

The Company Connection forum is an area that provides sales and marketing information on a bevvy of companies. Technology users can find help telephone numbers, product information, brochures and online service centers.
Berlow said that the minimum cost will start at about $4,800 a month and range up the hundreds of thousands of dollars, for the bigger companies.

"The big companies, where they have much more upside, should be treated like regular advertisers," Berlow said. He said AOL will try and find ways to make the charge affordable for smaller companies, who may not be able to afford the fee.
AOL said that the area is a mostly a promotional one and that AOL is bringing its eight million subscriber base to these firms who have, to date, had a presence there for free.
"These are areas where people sold things and did business," Berlow said. "When we reorganized our business, we thought this should be an advertising area."
He declined to give any forecast on what kind of revenues AOL could see from this area in the future.
AOL is seeking to derive more revenues from advertising and transactions and it saw an increase in its advertising revenues in its second quarter, which it reported earlier.
Some small firms are starting to protest AOL's decision to begin charging for the Company Connection.
Jeff Baudin, president of a small firm called MicroMat Computer Systems in Windsor, Calif., said that he is calling for a strike among the member companies of the area.

"The ones who are participating will black out our areas," he said, adding that his company has been part of Company Connection for seven years and he realizes it has been a "free ride." He is just hoping to reach some middle ground with AOL.
AOL's Berlow said he hopes any small businesses having a hard time with the costs will call him to work out a deal.
